title: Leaving Kirby for Duke Ellington's call in 1946
summary: The Copacabana closed, Kirby was missing for two weeks, and when Duke called, Procope took the job to make up lost time, not expecting to stay 28 years.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Now, you left him and went -- you left him in December, '45 -- or you joined him. No, you joined him in December, '45, but by the spring of '46 you seem to have been with Duke, so you weren't with him very long.

Oh, no, no, no, no, no, no, no. I couldn't take that, you know. And I couldn't -- in other words, doing what he was doing at that time wasn't furthering myself, wasn't in my groove, let's say, because there wasn't too much happening. And after the Copacabana closed, then I don't remember exactly, but sort of knocked around and knocked around, and then at one phase I couldn't find him for two weeks. I didn't even know where he was. He wasn't home. You know. So lo and behold, came this call from Duke Ellington. So by this time he was back, he appeared on the scene, and he offered me everything not to go with Duke. But I realized that he wasn't going anywhere at that time, and so I told him, I said, "Well, I just spent two years in the Army and I'm trying to get
back, you know, some of the two years I had lost. And I thought playing with Duke Ellington was a good way to do it. Not dreaming that I would be with Duke Ellington for 28 years.
I was going to say you didn't think you were going to stay there forever.
No. No. So anyway, I joined Duke Ellington.
